mainEntity.name: Does composite bonding require a consultation before treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A pre-treatment consultation is a standard and important part of the composite bonding process. During this appointment, the dentist assesses the health of your teeth, gums, and bite to determine whether composite bonding is suitable for your individual circumstances. It is also an opportunity to discuss your expectations and ask any questions about the treatment. Individual suitability is always determined through a clinical examination rather than based on general criteria alone.

mainEntity.name: Can composite bonding be done if I have existing fillings or dental work?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the specific situation and will be evaluated during your consultation. The presence of existing fillings or dental work does not automatically exclude composite bonding as an option, but it may influence the treatment plan. The dentist will assess the condition of existing restorations, their location, and whether they are likely to affect bonding. Each case is assessed individually during a clinical examination.

mainEntity.name: What happens if my gums aren't healthy when I come for a composite bonding consultation?

acceptedAnswer.text: If signs of gum disease are detected during your assessment, the dentist will typically recommend a course of gum treatment before cosmetic work proceeds. This might include a scale and polish or a more detailed periodontal assessment. Composite bonding on unhealthy gum tissue can be less predictable, as gum levels may change with treatment. Restoring gum health first supports a more stable and longer-lasting cosmetic outcome.

mainEntity.name: Will the dentist take X-rays before composite bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, yes. Dental X-rays allow the dentist to assess what is happening inside and between the teeth — areas not visible during a visual examination alone. X-rays can help detect early decay, assess root health, and identify any structural concerns that might influence treatment planning. Whether X-rays are taken will depend on when you last had radiographs and the clinical findings from your examination.

mainEntity.name: How long does a composite bonding assessment appointment typically take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Assessment appointments vary in length depending on how many teeth are being considered for treatment and how much clinical information needs to be gathered. In general, a composite bonding consultation may last between 30 minutes and an hour. Practices that include digital photography, shade matching, or smile design discussions may allocate longer appointments. Your dental practice will be able to advise you on what to expect before you attend.

mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding a permanent treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding is not considered a permanent treatment. The resin material is durable but may need maintenance, repair, or replacement over time — typically after several years, depending on the location of the bonding, the patient's bite, and their home care routine. Your dentist will discuss realistic expectations for longevity as part of your consultation. Good oral hygiene and attending regular dental reviews support the lifespan of composite bonding.
